name: mperft
_note: Switched from --bulk to --nullmove on 2026-05-27 — per upstream (talkchess viewtopic.php?t=86085) nullmove pruning is faster than plain bulk counting, because the player whose moves don't change the opponent's mobility (most moves at the last ply) can be batched into a single multiplication instead of a movegen. Wrapper re-spawns mperft per perft call, so a 4 GB hash table is freshly allocated each time (~1.6 s overhead). The with-cache modes still give honest deep-depth nps once work eclipses alloc — the runner's predictor was updated to skip extrapolation when last_elapsed < 1 s so cache modes can reach a meaningful depth.
